cubek.assessment: Algorithm reuse: plane sums plus shared partials, packed independent planes. No direct Cargo/API reuse: different CubeCL revision and ComputeClient/TensorBinding/runtime launch ownership; generic Inductor prologues/epilogues are replayed by our adapter.

cubecl_source.vector: VectorType, pointer reinterpretation, CompositeExtract/Construct; C++ typed-vector memory access; scalar semantic arithmetic and explicit lowp cast barriers retained
cubecl_source.plane: frontend/polyfills.rs sum expands into XOR shuffle offsets 1,2,4,8,16; checked plane dimension; CUDA shfl_sync uses active mask. Full participating planes and neutral inactive reduction values are required.
cubecl_source.policy: No compiler-invented coalescing/vectorization/reduction topology assumed. LLVM keeps conservative arithmetic flags; C++ NVRTC uses --fmad=false.

inductor.stride_analysis: Inspected tiling_utils CoalesceVarAnalysis and SIMD get_strides_of_load. Stage5 physical plans use the established typed direct-index descriptor, with exact affine runtime coefficient proofs rather than importing Triton tile/config objects. Historical config.triton.coalesce_tiling_analysis remains disabled for this experimental scalar logical schedule.
inductor.cache_discrepancy: PersistentCache.lookup actually invokes the benchmark callback on a miss independent of max_autotune_gemm; its docstring still describes the older gate.

aten.findings: ReduceConfig separates input/output cooperation, coalescing and vectorized loads; sum uses opmath FP32 for FP16/BF16. CUDA scalar opmath functors retain Python scalar literals in higher precision, independently of tensor storage dtype.
